expectations.text: Retrieves the Application resource and shows its sync and health status

expectations.text: Checks status conditions for errors (ComparisonError, SyncError)

expectations.text: Checks operation state for last sync result and error messages
expectations.evidence: status.operationState: Succeeded 'successfully synced (all tasks run)', plus status.sync.revision 8088f4c0… and the comparedTo/revision-vs-HEAD staleness check in the method.

expectations.text: Identifies which resources are out of sync or unhealthy
expectations.evidence: Lists status.resources (Service + Deployment kustomize-guestbook-ui, Synced/Healthy) and describes walking status.resources[] for Degraded entries.

expectations.text: Inspects the unhealthy managed resources (Deployments, Pods)

expectations.text: Checks pod logs or events for failing containers

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis (app does not exist; most likely a different instance's UI or an Application created in an unwatched namespace, backed by sourceNamespaces evidence) plus next steps and the method to apply on the real object.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies its current phase

expectations.text: Checks pause conditions (manual pause vs analysis-driven)
expectations.evidence: Concludes the halt is analysis-driven (steps[3] analysis, Error AnalysisRuns) rather than a manual pause, but never inspects status.pauseConditions / controllerPause for this Rollout as it does in eval 6.

expectations.text: Inspects associated AnalysisRuns if analysis is involved

expectations.text: Checks metric results and measurements in the AnalysisRun

expectations.text: Inspects traffic routing configuration if configured

expectations.text: Compares stable vs canary ReplicaSets and pod status
expectations.evidence: Revision tree shows the stable ReplicaSet and the ScaledDown rev-4 ReplicaSet, but there is no pod-level status comparison (no pod rows, no ready/restart counts for stable vs canary).

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations

expectations.text: Checks for argoproj.io CRDs on the cluster

expectations.text: Lists pods and their status in the Argo CD namespace

expectations.text: Inspects configuration (argocd-cm or ArgoCD CR)

expectations.text: Reports any unhealthy components with diagnostic details

expectations.text: Produces a structured status report
expectations.evidence: Numbered findings, an area-by-area health table (operator, webhook, each instance, rollouts, appset, control plane, routes/SSO) and an ordered remediation plan.

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and checks its status.conditions
expectations.evidence: Dumps conditions (ErrorOccurred=False, ParametersGenerated=True, ResourcesUpToDate=True) with lastTransitionTime 64 days stale, and explains that an empty generation is not an error so the CR self-reports green forever.

expectations.text: Identifies the generator type (git directory) and its configuration (repoURL, directories path pattern)
expectations.evidence: Prints spec.generators git block: repoURL alimobrem/agentit-gitops, revision HEAD, directories `apps/*` and the `apps/agentit` exclude, plus the template fields.

expectations.text: Lists currently generated Applications and cross-references against what's expected

expectations.text: Checks the applicationset-controller logs for generator errors
expectations.evidence: Controller log tail: allPaths="[apps]" total=1, 'generated 0 applications', 102ms reconcile, requeueAfter=3m0s, repeating with no errors; uses the 102ms/no-error signal to rule out auth and connectivity.

expectations.text: Identifies a likely cause (path pattern mismatch, repo access, or an exclude rule)
expectations.evidence: `apps/*` needs a segment under apps/ and the tree walk returned only `apps`; ranks wrong branch (HEAD→default branch), empty directories, wrong remote, stale cache — and explicitly eliminates the exclude rule as a red herring since exclusion is applied after the walk.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis with ranked causes, read-only verification commands (`git ls-remote --symref`, `git ls-tree -d`) and fixes (pin revision, commit real manifests, webhook, alert on 'generated 0 applications').

evals.name: ApplicationSet RollingSync stuck on production step

expectations.text: Retrieves the ApplicationSet and inspects spec.strategy.rollingSync.steps
expectations.evidence: `jq .spec` on the only ApplicationSet shows generators and template only — no strategy block — so the default AllAtOnce applies; states the described setup does not exist here.

expectations.text: Identifies which step/matchExpressions group production falls into
expectations.evidence: No steps exist. Explains that steps[].matchExpressions select on labels of the generated Application and that a missing `env: production` label in spec.template.metadata.labels makes the production step match zero apps — but no actual group is identified.

expectations.text: Checks whether the staging step's maxUpdate requirement and health gate have been satisfied
expectations.evidence: Names both gates generically (maxUpdate: 0 = unlimited, small values look slow; advancement requires Healthy AND Synced) but no maxUpdate value or gate state could be read from the cluster.

expectations.text: Debugs the staging Applications' health status, since an unhealthy staging app blocks progression to the next step
expectations.evidence: Points at status.applicationStatus[] as the per-app Waiting/Pending/Progressing/Healthy ladder to inspect for the straggler and the step it is attributed to, and shows it is absent here; no staging app health was actually debugged (zero Applications exist).

expectations.text: Explains how RollingSync blocks progression on unhealthy or unsynced apps in the current step
expectations.evidence: "RollingSync advances only when every Application in the current step is Healthy and Synced. One app stuck Progressing, or Synced+Degraded, blocks the whole wave indefinitely — there is no timeout." Also covers the automated-syncPolicy requirement and already-Synced skip.

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Primary root cause evidenced from the cluster (progressive-syncs feature flag absent from the appset controller env, argocd-cmd-params-cm and the ArgoCD CR, so RollingSync is parsed but never executed), six ranked secondary causes, a GitOps Promoter alternative with evidence, and fixes gated on the operator issue from eval 3.

evals.name: Blue-green rollout stuck at preview, never promotes

expectations.text: Retrieves the Rollout and identifies strategy.blueGreen configuration
expectations.evidence: `jq .spec.strategy` on bluegreen-demo (activeService, previewService, autoPromotionEnabled true, autoPromotionSeconds 30) plus status.blueGreen selectors, pauseConditions absent, observedGeneration.

expectations.text: Checks autoPromotionEnabled and explains that false requires manual promotion, not automatic analysis
expectations.evidence: Notes the real object is `true` (opposite of the prompt) and explains false means 'wait for a human, full stop' with BlueGreenPause/controllerPause, no timeout, cleared only by promote / spec change; adds that progressDeadlineSeconds does not govern this pause.

expectations.text: Checks for prePromotionAnalysis templates and their status if configured
expectations.evidence: Confirms neither prePromotionAnalysis nor postPromotionAnalysis exists in the spec, and gives the AnalysisRun query keyed on the preview pod hash to distinguish 'analysis never ran' from 'analysis failing'. Its claim that prePromotionAnalysis only runs when autoPromotionEnabled is true is questionable, but the check itself is performed.

expectations.text: Inspects previewService and activeService configuration for correctness
expectations.evidence: Lists both Services, shows activeSelector == previewSelector at revision 1 and explains why, and includes `oc get endpoints <previewService>` in the confirming commands plus 'verify previewService has endpoints and both Services exist' as a separate failure mode.

expectations.text: Distinguishes blue-green behavior from canary (no step-based automatic progression)
expectations.evidence: "Unlike canary — where an analysis entry in steps[] makes the gate obvious — blue-green runs analysis only if strategy.blueGreen.prePromotionAnalysis.templates[] is populated."

expectations.text: Produces a report with root cause and recommendations
expectations.evidence: Root cause framed as a configuration misconception with two independent explanations, three alternative fixes by intent, the preview-Service check, and a caveat about the flapping rollouts controller on this cluster.

evals.name: Ambiguous debug request with multiple Argo CD instances

expectations.text: Detects multiple Argo CD instances (multiple namespaces with argocd-labeled pods or multiple ArgoCD CRs)
expectations.evidence: `oc get argocd -A` returns three CRs, corroborated by three distinct Routes.

expectations.text: Lists all detected instances with their namespaces
expectations.evidence: Table of instance / namespace / scope / app count / appset controller / rollouts / route TLS, with the route hostnames listed separately.

expectations.text: Asks the user which instance to investigate, or investigates all and clearly separates findings per instance
expectations.evidence: Works through all three, establishes scope from operator env vars and cluster secrets, verifies no namespace is claimed by two instances, and attributes each finding to its instance (stray argocd instance in the operator namespace, team-b insecure edge route, invalid Rollout in openshift-gitops).

expectations.text: Does not silently pick one instance without disclosing the ambiguity
expectations.evidence: "Answer to 'which instance?' — None of them individually; the fault is shared infrastructure" (operator + control plane), with the multi-instance 'my app isn't showing up' explanation added.

expectations.text: Produces a report structured per instance
expectations.evidence: Per-instance comparison table plus findings each labelled with the owning instance and an ordered remediation list; organised by fault with instance attribution rather than strictly instance-by-instance sections.

expectations.text: Retrieves the Application and identifies health.status as Suspended
expectations.evidence: Confirms no billing-service and no finance namespace and that the only Application is Synced/Healthy, not Suspended; the literal state does not exist to identify.

expectations.text: Explains that Suspended reflects an intentionally paused resource (e.g. a paused CronJob or Rollout), not a failure
expectations.evidence: "A first-class, healthy status in Argo CD's health model — not an error", listing suspended CronJob, paused Deployment/Rollout, BlueGreenPause and suspended Job, with 'Degraded is the failure status'. (It also ranks sync windows first as a cause of a 'suspended-looking' app, which conflates sync-window denial with Suspended health.)

expectations.text: Inspects the underlying managed resource to identify what is suspended and why
expectations.evidence: Supplies the resource-walk one-liner over status.resources to find the suspended child and says the fix for a paused Rollout is to promote it; inspects the live AppProject sync windows instead, since no suspended managed resource exists on the cluster.

expectations.text: Does not treat Suspended as an error requiring remediation unless the user confirms it's unintended
expectations.evidence: "Why I'd push back on 'the team thinks it's broken'" — all three causes are intended states and remediation is usually explanation or promotion, not repair.

expectations.text: Produces a report distinguishing intentional suspension from a genuine problem
expectations.evidence: Separates intended suspension from the one genuine defect it does flag with evidence (example-team sync windows with no manualSync and no timeZone, evaluated in UTC, currently outside the allow window), with scoped fixes.

evals.name: Multi-source Application with one failing source

expectations.text: Detects the Application uses spec.sources[] (multi-source), not spec.source
expectations.evidence: `jq '.spec | keys'` shows singular spec.source and status.sourceType (not sourceTypes); confirms via `oc explain applications.argoproj.io.spec.sources` that the field exists but is unused, and warns the unqualified `oc explain applications.spec.sources` resolves to the app.k8s.io CRD.

expectations.text: Iterates every entry in spec.sources[] individually, checking repoURL, targetRevision, path, and Helm valueFiles for each
expectations.evidence: Gives an indexed enumeration over spec.sources printing repoURL, chart/path, targetRevision and ref, with helm valueFiles/$values wiring covered in the per-source failure-mode analysis; no entries existed to iterate.

expectations.text: Identifies which specific source is failing (e.g. wrong values file path, inaccessible repo, or bad targetRevision)
expectations.evidence: No failing source exists. Provides strong localisation technique (status.sourceTypes shorter than spec.sources → first missing index is the broken source; per-source revisions in operationState.syncResult; conditions naming the repoURL; repo-server log filtered by repo host) and six ranked failure modes, but identifies no specific source.

expectations.text: Does not treat a multi-source Application as if it were single-source
expectations.evidence: Treats sources as an indexed array throughout ('the ordinal is how everything else is keyed'), with ref/$values semantics, per-source credentials and AppProject sourceRepos restrictions handled per source.

expectations.text: Produces a report identifying the specific failing source and the fix
expectations.evidence: Method, ranked failure modes with fixes, and cluster-specific caveats (no repository secrets, example-team sourceRepos allow-list, sync windows, which instance's repo-server to read), but states plainly there is nothing to fix because the Application does not exist — no specific source identified.
